reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's goal to help the Hebrew people through multiple elements: (1) God directly commands Moses to send spies to Canaan 'אשר אני נתן לבני ישראל' ('which I am giving to the children of Israel'), establishing the land-gift as central to His plan; (2) The promised land is described as flowing 'milk and honey,' emphasizing its value as a blessing; (3) Despite the people's rebellion and lack of faith, God's response—while including judgment on the unfaithful generation—promises to bring their children into the land ('וידעו את־הארץ אשר מאסתם בה'); (4) God affirms His commitment to Israel's future possession of the land even through the judgment narrative. The entire passage is structured around Yahweh's persistent goal to establish Israel in their promised homeland. Though God disciplines unfaithfulness, He never abandons His ultimate purpose of helping Israel inherit and possess the land.
